newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police quiz IRA suspect.
newsitem.headline: Irish police quiz IRA suspect.

text.p: Irish police questioned three people including British extradition target Nessan Qunilivan on Monday about membership of the outlawed Irish Republican Army (IRA).
They were arrested in an early morning police operation in the southwestern town of Limerick and detained under emergency provisions allowing them to be held for up to 48 hours.
Police said they were being questioned about membership of the IRA, which is fighting British rule of Northern Ireland, but gave no further details or names.
IRA membership is illegal in the Irish Republic as well as in Northern Ireland and Britain.
Quinlivan was released on bail by the High Court in Dublin last year while awaiting an appeal against British attempts to extradite him.

Quinlivan and fellow IRA suspect Pearse McAuley shot their way out of London's Brixton prison using a smuggled gun in 1991 while awaiting trial on charges of conspiracy to murder and cause explosions.
Britain said the two were involved in an IRA plot to murder brewing tycoon Sir Charles Tidbury.

Both men fled to Ireland where they were jailed on firearms charges but were released last year as part of the Irish government's early release programme to reward the IRA for a ceasefire it declared in August 1994.
They were immediately re-arrested in connection with Britain's extradition request but freed pending their appeal.
